sentences.text: Ms.Amrita Singh, Advocate for the complainant.

The petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita, 2023 with a prayer to grant anticipatory bail to him in case Fir No.141 dated 21.09.2024,
registered under Sections 420 of Ipc and Section 13 of the Punjab Travel Professionals (Regulation)
Act, 2014 at Police Station Dinanagar, District Gurdaspur.

2. At the very outset, learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the petitioner has settled the
dispute with respondent No.2/complainant in the present case.

3. On the other hand, short reply by way of an affidavit of Assistant Superintendent of Police,
Dinanagar, District Gurdaspur has been filed on behalf of the respondent-State in Court today and
the same is taken on record.

4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2/complainant submits that the petitioner has amicably resolved the dispute 1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:035146 with respondent No.2 and the payment has already been made to the complainant and she has no objection if the present petition is allowed.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6. In fact, it appears that there was a financial disputes between the parties and since the parties have amicably resolved their disputes, the present petition is allowed.
The petitioner is granted concession of anticipatory bail, subject to the conditions as provided under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.

It will be open for the Investigating Officer to call the petitioner to join investigation, if so required, by issuing a written notice in this regard and he shall abide by the conditions mentioned in Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
